provisionalMaterialIssues: The answer says the supplied evidence does not include the general residential R503.1 exception text in full and therefore cannot establish whether another residential exception applies. Source ECC R503, in research-permitext_discovered-id:33000020-3 and -6, supplies the exception list, including its roof-recover item and the other listed items; the claim that the text is incomplete is contradicted by the supplied source. This also makes the recommendation to obtain the complete residential exception text unnecessary.

The advice not to leave the sill-gap portion uninsulated if ECC R503.1.1.3 applies does not account for ECC R402.5.1.1, which says insulation is not required in the rough-opening gap between window framing and the window frame, except as required by the fenestration manufacturer’s instructions. Because the answer does not distinguish that gap from an exposed wall cavity, its advice could lead to a different conclusion for the installation asked about. Relevant supplied sources: sectionID 33000011, sourceID research-permitext_discovered-id:33000011-2 (ECC R402.5.1.1); sectionID 33000020, sourceID research-permitext_discovered-id:33000020-4 (ECC R503.1.1.3).

The decisive LPC approval and design-acceptability rule is absent, so the answer cannot determine whether the proposed replicas may be installed. This is a material evidence gap, not an unsupported conclusion: the answer expressly limits its conclusion to what the supplied sources establish.

provisionalMaterialIssues: The answer cites ECC §R402.1.3’s R-49 ceiling value but omits ECC §R402.2.2. That section permits a minimum R-38 for certain ceilings without attics when a roof/ceiling assembly cannot fit a required value above R-38, subject to a 500-square-foot-or-20-percent area limit and an exclusion for the component-performance alternative. If the raised rafter area meets those conditions, this could affect whether another material can meet the applicable requirement; the answer does not flag or assess that possibility.
